laws.name: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
laws.principle: Users often perceive aesthetically pleasing design as design that’s more usable.
applies_when: New visual styling, layout or component
violation_heuristics: Hardcoded colors, fonts or spacing that bypass design tokens or CSS variables
Misaligned or inconsistent spacing values (e.g. 13px next to 16px scale)
Screenshot: visual clutter, clashing colors, broken alignment

laws.name: Choice Overload
laws.principle: The tendency for people to get overwhelmed when they are presented with a large number of options, often used interchangeably with the term paradox of choice.
applies_when: Menus, selects, filters, pricing tiers, product grids
violation_heuristics: More than ~7 equal weight options in one select, menu or filter group without grouping or search
Option lists with no default or recommended choice
Screenshot: grid of many equal choices with no hierarchy

laws.name: Chunking
laws.principle: A process by which individual pieces of an information set are broken down and then grouped together in a meaningful whole.
violation_heuristics: Long forms or content blocks without fieldsets, headings or sections
Long numbers (phone, card, codes) shown or entered as one unbroken string
Walls of text over ~5 lines with no subheads or lists

laws.name: Cognitive Bias
laws.principle: A systematic error of thinking or rationality in judgment that influence our perception of the world and our decision-making ability.
applies_when: Consent, pricing, upsell, checkout, CTA copy
violation_heuristics: Pre-checked opt-in checkboxes for marketing or paid add-ons
Confirmshaming copy on decline buttons
Fake urgency or scarcity (hardcoded countdowns, static 'only 2 left')

laws.name: Cognitive Load
laws.principle: The amount of mental resources needed to understand and interact with an interface.
violation_heuristics: Inputs without visible labels (placeholder as label)
Many competing CTAs or font sizes in one view
Unexplained icons without text or aria-label
Required info hidden behind hover only

laws.name: Doherty Threshold
laws.principle: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that neither has to wait on the other.
violation_heuristics: Async action (submit, add to cart, fetch) with no loading, pending or optimistic state
Blocking synchronous scripts, large unoptimized images, missing width/height or lazy loading
Animations or transitions longer than ~400ms on core interactions

laws.name: Fitts's Law
laws.principle: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target.
violation_heuristics: Tap targets under 44x44px (CSS width/height/padding)
Primary action placed far from related input or at an unexpected edge
Small inline links as the only way to perform a key action
Destructive action adjacent to primary with no spacing

laws.name: Flow
laws.principle: The mental state in which a person performing some activity is fully immersed in a feeling of energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment in the process of the activity.
violation_heuristics: Unnecessary interruptions: modals or popups on load, forced signup mid task
No feedback after user action (silent success or failure)
Navigation that resets user progress or scroll position

laws.name: Goal-Gradient Effect
laws.principle: The tendency to approach a goal increases with proximity to the goal.
violation_heuristics: Multi step flow (checkout, onboarding, form wizard) with no progress indicator
Progress indicator that does not reflect real remaining steps

laws.name: Hick's Law
laws.principle: The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.
violation_heuristics: Navigation or menu with more than ~7 top level items
Several primary styled buttons in one view
Complex decision screens without a recommended path

laws.name: Jakob's Law
laws.principle: Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know.
violation_heuristics: Nonstandard placement of logo, cart, search or account
Links not styled as links or buttons not styled as buttons
Custom controls replacing native ones without matching behavior (keyboard, focus)
Unconventional icons for common actions

laws.name: Law of Common Region
laws.principle: Elements tend to be perceived into groups if they are sharing an area with a clearly defined boundary.
violation_heuristics: Related controls or info not enclosed in a shared container, card or fieldset
Containers that group unrelated items

laws.name: Law of Proximity
laws.principle: Objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together.
violation_heuristics: Label farther from its input than from neighboring inputs
Uniform spacing between unrelated groups and related items
Helper or error text detached from its field

laws.name: Law of Similarity
laws.principle: The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if those elements are separated.
violation_heuristics: Same style used for elements with different functions (links and plain text same color)
Different styles for elements of the same function (inconsistent button classes)

laws.name: Law of Uniform Connectedness
laws.principle: Elements that are visually connected are perceived as more related than elements with no connection.
violation_heuristics: Related steps or items with no visual connector (line, shared background, border) when relation matters
Visual connectors linking unrelated elements

laws.name: Mental Model
laws.principle: A compressed model based on what we think we know about a system and how it works.
violation_heuristics: Labels or icons that contradict common meaning (e.g. trash icon that archives)
Terminology inconsistent with the rest of the product
Interaction that behaves unlike similar elements elsewhere in the codebase

laws.name: Miller's Law
laws.principle: The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory.
violation_heuristics: Lists, tabs or nav exposing more than ~9 ungrouped items at once
Requiring users to remember info from a prior screen (codes, IDs)

laws.name: Occam's Razor
laws.principle: Among competing hypotheses that predict equally well, the one with the fewest assumptions should be selected.
violation_heuristics: Added wrappers, options or steps without clear user value
Duplicate controls for the same action in one view
Decorative elements that compete with content

laws.name: Paradox of the Active User
laws.principle: Users never read manuals but start using the software immediately.
violation_heuristics: Feature that only works after reading instructions or docs
Essential guidance only in a dismissible tour or tooltip
Empty states with no inline hint or action

laws.name: Pareto Principle
laws.principle: The Pareto principle states that, for many events, roughly 80% of the effects come from 20% of the causes.
violation_heuristics: Primary action or most used content buried below secondary content
Equal visual weight for core and rarely used actions

laws.name: Parkinson's Law
laws.principle: Any task will inflate until all of the available time is spent.
violation_heuristics: Forms asking for optional or unnecessary fields
Missing autofill/autocomplete attributes on standard inputs (name, email, address)
Extra confirmation steps that do not prevent real errors

laws.name: Peak-End Rule
laws.principle: People judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak and at its end, rather than the total sum or average of every moment of the experience.
violation_heuristics: Success or completion state removed, generic or missing (e.g. after purchase or submit)
Error states with raw or blaming messages
Abrupt endings with no next step

laws.name: Postel's Law
laws.principle: Be liberal in what you accept, and conservative in what you send.
applies_when: Inputs, forms, responsive layout, data rendering
violation_heuristics: Strict input validation rejecting valid formats (spaces in phone, case in email)
Missing inputmode, type or autocomplete hints
Layout that breaks with long text, translations or small viewports (fixed widths, no wrapping)
No handling for empty, null or error data

laws.name: Selective Attention
laws.principle: The process of focusing our attention only to a subset of stimuli in an environment — usually those related to our goals.
violation_heuristics: Important notices styled like ads or banners users ignore
Key message competing with motion or high contrast decoration
Critical status shown only via color

laws.name: Serial Position Effect
laws.principle: Users have a propensity to best remember the first and last items in a series.
violation_heuristics: Most important nav items or actions placed in the middle of a list
Key info buried in the middle of long content

laws.name: Tesler's Law
laws.principle: Tesler's Law, also known as The Law of Conservation of Complexity, states that for any system there is a certain amount of complexity which cannot be reduced.
violation_heuristics: Complexity pushed to user that the system could handle (manual formatting, unit conversion, retyping known data)
Removing defaults or smart handling

laws.name: Von Restorff Effect
laws.principle: The Von Restorff effect, also known as The Isolation Effect, predicts that when multiple similar objects are present, the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered.
violation_heuristics: Primary CTA not visually distinct from secondary actions
Too many highlighted elements so none stands out
Emphasis relying on color only (no shape, weight or text)

laws.name: Working Memory
laws.principle: A cognitive system that temporarily holds and manipulates information needed to complete tasks.
violation_heuristics: Instructions or context removed from the screen where they are needed
Validation errors shown only after submit, away from fields
Comparisons requiring switching between pages or tabs

laws.name: Zeigarnik Effect
laws.principle: People remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks better than completed tasks.
violation_heuristics: Incomplete tasks (cart, form, profile) with no saved state or reminder
Progress lost on refresh or navigation
